scores.strengths: Only design with a real numerical prototype through the actual engine: chunk invariance exact to 0.0 across chunk_symbols/chunk_days on six roots, which is the one property the daily-leaf work can silently get wrong. Only design that catches the Partura-side cache: PanelSet.view_id (partura/panels.py:216) is store_path|start|end|len(symbols)|dates[0]|dates[-1] and _cache_path = sha1(view_id|expr_key) (panels.py:222), so a daily-field rebuild serves a stale on-disk panel for every DF:-bearing expression -- a plausible wrong number, not an error, which is the class of bug that costs the loop a week. Its registry inventory is the only correct one: I measured 29 boolean_output, 22 trivial_boolean, coarse_output empty, and it is the only design that names the full mis-flag set {in_sustain_mean, in_sustain_stddev, in_sustain_product} (the other two name two and one). declare_real_valued(*names) is the right separation: it lets Partura clear flags on kernels whose definition site it does not own. Smallest diff of the three (~250 lines + a build script) and it says itself that WP1-WP4 should be one commit.
scores.flaws: 1. _pick_weighted does NOT reproduce Partura's pick, contrary to its own claim that it does 'exactly' so 'the migration changes no behaviour'. It computes a face's weight as sum(ws)/len(ws) over the FULL face including zeros; idea_search.py:205-206 builds `faces` from w>0 specs only and divides by that positive count. I ran the two: a face with 2 live of 10 gives Partura 1.0 and minimal-diff 0.2 -- a 5x distortion of face balance. WP11's acceptance step ('the control arm should reproduce its earlier trajectory') therefore fails, and the failure reads as a bug somewhere else. 2. strict_accept's default (None -> accept is not None) makes the two A/B arms differ in ban enforcement: its own migration gives the control arm SearchHooks(op_weight=base_weight_only) -> no accept -> strict_accept False -> mutate_window/mutate_constant keep the leak, while the steer arm gets accept -> fix on. Under the user's standing --ban/--ban-archive de-correlation rule the arms then differ by two things, contradicting its own sentence 'the arms are now genuinely identical except for the intervention'. 3. The scorer factory signature is factory(target, dates=..., turnover_penalty=...) -- no daily, no trim, no symbols. So requirement 甲's reward-bucketing leg is not served by AlphaCube at all, and dates without trim walks straight into the grid trap (see must_fix 6). 4. GP leaf sampling is explicitly out of scope ('Nothing in WP1-WP9 adds DailyFeature to TypedTreeGenerator.fields'), so after 11 work packages the search still cannot discover cs_bucket_rank(x, FloatCap) -- only a human can type it. Two of the three uses my brief asks about are deferred. 5. 'The report's generations then reflects what actually ran, which it already does (it is derived, not assumed)' is false: gp.py:786 is report.generations = n_gen, assigned unconditionally, so a wall_seconds break over-reports and corrupts the per-generation efficiency denominator the A/B reads. 6. WP2's AlphaCube test table names cs_bucket_rank and the text names cs_winsor; both are Partura operators (ops_ext.py:232, 718-722), absent from default_registry(). Those tests cannot be written as specified.

scores.strengths: Least glue of the three, and I verified the mechanism: pipeline.py:361-368 does gp = dict(...); gp.update(gp_params or {}); GPMiner(..., **gp), so operator_weights / accept_hook / wall_clock_budget need ZERO new run_mining parameters -- and idea_search.py:260 already builds exactly that dict. The migration is 'add three keys'. Its weighted _pick is the only one that is a true drop-in for Partura's monkeypatch: it filters the pool to w>0 first and then divides by len(wf[n]) (the positive count), byte-equivalent to idea_search.py:204-207, so both arms reproduce their pre-migration trajectories and the migration is auditable against episode e1. gen.hook_rng is the single biggest reproducibility fix on offer: it provides a separate random.Random and states the migration must move idea_search.py:231's G.accept(e, u=self._rng.random()) off the shared stream -- today that draw is data-dependent, so no steer-arm run is reproducible from its seed. mutation_checks_bans defaults to True, so the mutate_window/mutate_constant fix is on for BOTH arms with False as the replay lever -- the right default, unlike minimal-diff. Shape.daily_only makes the no-minute-axis rule a property of the value rather than an isinstance inside a predicate, so GeneralCall's own operand_ok loop (expression.py:318-322, the research/legacy surface) is covered by the same edit. Verified correct on needs_full_m = (face=='dt' and family in ('in','day')) or face=='nt' (axes.py:89-91) and on non_root = boolean_output or coarse_output (axes.py:113-114), which is why one real_valued declaration clears both the vocabulary filter and the root gate.
scores.flaws: 1. The registry latch breaks its own test plan. op() raises once build_registry has returned, conftest.py's `registry` fixture is session-scoped (tests/conftest.py:8-9), and WP-H5 asks for 'real_valued=True on a throwaway @op' in the same pytest process as WP-H4's 'THE LATCH: after default_registry(), a fresh @op raises RuntimeError'. Those two tests cannot both pass, and no reset hook is offered. 2. Its own risk [7] is the blocker: the latch 'will fire on real code the first time', and the code it names is scripts/idea_search.py, which imports ops_ext at module level (line 44) and parses seeds through parse(G.canonical(s), ...) at line ~245. Imposing a call-order change on the loop's hottest file while B01's 15 ideas are mid-batch is a poor trade. 3. Mis-flag set undercounted by two: it names only in_sustain_stddev and says the vocabulary grows 'by one'. I measured in_sustain_mean, in_sustain_stddev and in_sustain_product all boolean_output AND trivial_boolean, so the real delta is +3 (214->217 default, 218->221 with allow_resource_risk=True, which is what Partura runs). WP-H6's 'exact trivial_boolean set before and after' test is written against the wrong set. 4. No daily and no trim in the scorer contract -- its kw list is turnover_penalty/signed/cost_per_side/top_frac/min_coverage/min_scored_days AND dates, nothing else. Its risk [10] names the warm-up hazard and then leaves it to a docstring, which is exactly the hazard that matters (must_fix 6). 5. Its stated justification for construction-time weight validation is mis-attributed: weights do not filter self.specs, so zeroing every reduces_m operator cannot reach self._rng.choice(sorted({})) -- _pick_weighted's all-zero fallback returns a uniform draw instead, meaning a crippled weight table silently un-steers rather than crashing. The validation is still worth having (it becomes essential the moment a vocabulary drop-set is grafted), but the failure mode as written does not exist. 6. GP leaf sampling is WP-H7, optional and thin, with no positional hint, so FloatCap-in-the-key-slot remains undiscoverable. 7. in_mean(FloatCap, 5) appears in the test table; in_mean is not in default_registry().

scores.strengths: The only design that closes all three daily-field uses my brief asks about. Hypothesis expressions: parse + evaluate. Reward bucketing: ScorerContext.daily['FloatCap'] returns (D,S) on the target's own grid, so the leaf layer and the reward layer read one object. Search leaves: daily_leaf_prob in _gen plus leaf_slots positional hints in _build. The leaf_slots insight is correct and non-obvious -- I confirmed _operand_reqs returns ('daily','daily') for an nd pair (generator.py:317-323), so without a positional hint the GP has no way to know operand 1 of cs_bucket_rank is the KEY and will put a tree there as often as a field; without that one line 'rank x inside its own cap decile' is expressible but undiscoverable, which is the entire point of FloatCap. ScorerContext is the only contract carrying trim, and split_at() is literally Partura's existing cut = searchsorted(dates, SPLIT) idiom while panel_grid_matches() promotes ParturaScorer's hand-rolled shape+finite-mask assertion into something every factory gets free. One factory keyed by req.arm produces both arms, replacing install(arm)'s two class-method rebinds and the finally restore (idea_search.py:239, 274) -- the exact place 'the arms differ only by the intervention' stops being true -- and --arm both collapses the A/B to one command. It is also the only design right on four behavioural facts I checked: report.generations = n_gen must become done_gen (gp.py:786); make_scorer's unregistered kind should keep falling through to PanelScorer so the same ValueError('kind must be ic or rank_ic') comes from the same place (scoring.py:46-47, 515-520); test_mining.py:376-385 already loops over mutate_window/mutate_constant and asserts the fixed behaviour, so the 乙.2 fix makes an existing test meaningful (and it asks to see it fail pre-fix); and rankban.view_cache_key hashes only dates[0]|dates[-1]|len|n_symbols|samples with no store identity (rankban.py:242-249). Keeping --fitness choices=scorer_kinds() accurate by pre-parsing --plugin with parse_known_args is a small thing a researcher touches every run.
scores.flaws: 1. Vocabulary numbers wrong: it claims 'in_sustain_mean AND in_sustain_stddev ... the fact map named one kernel; there are two' and pins 214->216. There are three (in_sustain_product too), so the delta is 214->217; and 214 is searchable(include_boolean=False, include_resource_risk=False) whereas Partura runs allow_resource_risk=True where the baseline is 218. tests/test_vocabulary_size.py::test_searchable_count == 216 fails on arrival. 2. _pick_weighted divides a face's weight by the full face size (sum(ws)/len(ws)) where Partura divides by the positive count (idea_search.py:205-206) -- 1.0 vs 0.2 in the case I ran. It does not claim equivalence, but it means the migrated steer arm's distribution shifts and e1's numbers stop being comparable, and nothing in the plan notices. 3. Steering.control() returns Steering(drop_ops=..., note=...) with op_weights dropped, so the control arm moves to the unweighted choice path -- while today's control arm also goes through choices (idea_search.py's pick runs for both arms, with base_weight only). Its risk [2] honestly states the arms cannot share a stream, but misses the consequence: the CONTROL arm also stops reproducing its pre-migration trajectory, so the migration has no anchor to be validated against. 4. Largest surface by far: 18 work packages, Steering (9 fields) + SteeringRequest (8) + ScorerContext (12), three registries and 10 new mine flags, landed mid-batch. Its own set_context wrinkle concedes the 'one command, no driver script' promise does not arrive in round 1, so the loop pays the full build cost for a partial payoff. 5. DailyFieldView caches both panel() and panel_ds() per field (2x40 MB, ~490 MB for six) next to the 6 GiB panel_cache_bytes Partura already configures (idea_search.py:261) in a container that has been OOM-killed before; release() exists and nothing calls it. Risk [4] says so and leaves it. 6. Default --ffill-limit 5 on the cap fields, which the other two refuse, guaranteeing the new planes disagree with Partura's existing unfilled ones (must_fix 7). 7. AC-2's AlphaCube test asks to parse 'each table expression in the daily_fields section', and that table contains cs_bucket_rank (a Partura operator); in_mean(FloatCap, 5) also does not exist.

graft: From search-usability: ScorerContext as the scorer factory's single argument, carrying target, dates, symbols, trim, daily and options plus split_at() and panel_grid_matches(). It replaces typed-correctness's factory(target, **kw) bag of keywords. split_at() is Partura's existing searchsorted(ps.dates, SPLIT) idiom and trim is what closes the grid trap in must_fix 6; ctx.daily['FloatCap'] is what makes requirement 甲's reward-bucketing leg real instead of leaving Partura to load cap a second way.

From search-usability: Steering.leaf_slots, i.e. {'cs_bucket_rank': {1: ('FloatCap',)}, 'cs_bucket_demean': {1: ('FloatCap',)}, 'cs_bucket_zscore': {1: ('FloatCap',)}} consulted in _build. Verified necessary: _operand_reqs (generator.py:317-323) returns ('daily','daily') for an nd pair, so the bucket-key slot is positionally blind and the GP fills it with a random daily tree. Without this one line the headline factor shape is expressible and undiscoverable.

From search-usability: daily_leaf_prob short-circuited in _gen's depth<=1 branch as `if self._daily_fields and self._rng.random() < self._daily_leaf_prob:` -- the empty-list short circuit is what keeps the RNG stream untouched when off. Promote typed-correctness's WP-H7 from optional to required; without it the daily fields never reach the third of my brief's three places.

From search-usability: keep --fitness choices=scorer_kinds() accurate by pre-parsing --plugin with an add_help=False parser and parse_known_args before build_parser(), instead of deleting choices= (cli.py:330) and moving validation downstream. --help and shell completion stay correct, which matters on a flag used every run.

From search-usability: leave make_scorer's unregistered-kind path falling through to the existing PanelScorer(target, kind=kind, ...) call so the same ValueError('kind must be ic or rank_ic', scoring.py:46-47) comes out of the same place. Drop typed-correctness's switch to KeyError, which is a gratuitous behaviour change on a path tests may observe directly.

From search-usability: report.generations = done_gen plus report.stopped_early (fixes gp.py:786); the rankban.view_cache_key store-identity fix (rankban.py:242-249); and the discipline of showing tests/test_mining.py::test_banned_substructures_cannot_enter_by_any_route FAIL on the pre-fix code before landing the mutate_window/mutate_constant change, since that test already covers it and passes today only by luck.

From search-usability: an arm selector (--arm both / steering_arm) so both A/B arms are produced by one factory keyed by arm, with the control transform idempotent. This is what retires install(arm)'s rebinding of TypedTreeGenerator._pick/.acceptable and the finally restore at idea_search.py:239,274 -- but keep typed-correctness's weighted _pick on BOTH arms (see must_fix 3) rather than search-usability's control() that drops op_weights.

From minimal-diff: the PanelSet.view_id fix (partura/panels.py:216) -- mix the daily store's identity into it, since _cache_path keys on sha1(view_id|expr_key) and nothing in view_id moves when the daily fields are rebuilt. Also reuse its prototype at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/design/proto_daily_leaf.py, re-run with its monkeypatches deleted against the real implementation, as the chunk-invariance acceptance gate.

From minimal-diff: declare_real_valued(*names) as a by-name override channel alongside the @op(real_valued=True) definition-site flag, so a plugin can clear flags on AlphaCube's own three in_sustain_* kernels without owning their definition -- cleaner than typed-correctness's single mechanism and than Partura's current dataclasses.replace loop.

From minimal-diff: its measured flag inventory as the exact-set regression test (29 boolean_output, 22 trivial_boolean, coarse_output empty), with the corrected three-name mis-flag set. No test pins these today, which is why both mis-flag families are silent.
must_fix: The real-valued mis-flag set is {in_sustain_mean, in_sustain_stddev, in_sustain_product} -- I measured all three as boolean_output AND trivial_boolean (in_sustain itself is genuinely boolean and stays). Baselines: searchable(include_boolean=False, include_resource_risk=False) = 214 (the generator/Vocabulary default, what tests/test_planted_signal.py runs on) and searchable(include_boolean=False) = 218 (resource_risk included, which is what Partura runs with allow_resource_risk=True). Declaring the three moves 214->217 and 218->221. Every design's figure is wrong (minimal-diff 218->220 for three names, typed-correctness 'by one', search-usability 214->216), so all three pin-the-exact-set tests fail on arrival. Fix the set and state both baselines, because the trajectory break lands differently for the default suite than for Partura's runs.

gp.py:786 is `report.generations = n_gen`, assigned unconditionally, not derived. Any wall-clock / early-stop budget must set it to the count actually completed and expose stopped_early, or the per-generation and per-100-evaluation efficiency denominators the A/B comparison reads are silently inflated. minimal-diff asserts the opposite of the source here.

The weighted _pick's face weight must use the positive-weight denominator -- sum(w for positive) / len(positive) -- matching idea_search.py:205-206. minimal-diff and search-usability both divide by the full face size; I ran it and a face with 2 live operators of 10 gets 1.0 under Partura and 0.2 under theirs. Only typed-correctness is right. This is not cosmetic: it is the only thing that lets a post-migration control (or steer) arm be diffed against episode e1 to prove the migration changed nothing, and minimal-diff's WP11 explicitly plans that diff.

The mutate_window / mutate_constant ban fix must be ON for both A/B arms by default. typed-correctness (mutation_checks_bans=True) and search-usability (unconditional) do this; minimal-diff's strict_accept default of `None -> (accept is not None)` leaves the leak open in the control arm (no accept hook) and closed in the steer arm, so under the standing --ban / --ban-archive de-correlation rule the arms differ by two things rather than one. Keep a single explicit flag for bit-exact replay of old banned runs, never a default that varies by arm.

The accept hook must not draw from the generator's RNG. Provide gen.hook_rng (typed-correctness) or require the plugin's own random.Random seeded from the request (search-usability), and change idea_search.py:231's `G.accept(e, u=self._rng.random())`. Today that draw is consumed a data-dependent number of times inside acceptable(), so no steer-arm run is reproducible from its seed and re-running a promising episode under a slightly different ban set reproduces nothing. minimal-diff does not mention this at all.

The scorer contract must carry trim (and symbols), not only dates. Verified: PanelSet.dates = view.dates[trim:] (partura/panels.py:172) and ps.target(1) returns full[trim:] (panels.py:248), while run_mining's target is over the untrimmed warmed view (pipeline.py:244-246). They match today only because START=20180102 is the store's first date, so warmed_view's `d0 = max(0, base.d0 - warmup)` gives trim=0 (research.py:85-86). Move --start later -- which any rolling or blocked study does -- and ParturaScorer's own `target.shape != ctx.tgt.shape` assertion raises inside run_mining, where idea_search.py's bare `except Exception` turns it into a printed line and an arm that silently produces nothing. Only search-usability passes trim; the other two pass dates and document the hazard.

scripts/build_daily_fields.py duplicates /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/build_shared.py, which already reads the same /root/autodl-tmp/qmt_daily_data/daily_capital parquet via tearsheet.load_caps over the same store axes and writes log_float_cap.npy, log_total_cap.npy and log_turnover_rate.npy -- and whose docstring states the same motivation ('F001 could not tell low turnover from small cap because the cube only has Amt'). No design notices. Pick one source of truth and one convention before writing the script: build_shared stores log, the designs store raw float32 (minimal-diff's own risk #2 notes a 1e12 cap quantises to ~1e5 yuan in float32, so ts_delta(FloatCap, 1) is representation noise at short horizons); build_shared does no fill, minimal-diff and typed-correctness refuse to fill, search-usability ffills 5 days by default; build_shared drops the warm-up rows (view.dates[trim:]) while the daily store spans the full axes. Otherwise the loop carries two disagreeing cap panels, and log_turnover_rate.npy already IS the div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap) motivating example.

New AlphaCube test tables must use operators AlphaCube actually has. Verified against default_registry(): cs_bucket_rank, cs_bucket_demean, cs_bucket_zscore and cs_winsor are Partura's (partura/ops_ext.py:232, 405, 424, 718-722) and in_mean does not exist. minimal-diff's WP2 table and text name cs_bucket_rank and cs_winsor; search-usability's AC-2 asks to parse its whole daily_fields table including cs_bucket_rank; both it and typed-correctness use in_mean(FloatCap, 5). Only typed-correctness flags the substitution ('using a built-in nd binary when Partura is absent'). The bucket-key behaviour has to be tested in Partura's suite, or with a throwaway nd pair kernel registered in AlphaCube's.

Two caches are blind to the daily store's identity and both must mix it in: AlphaCube's rankban.view_cache_key (rankban.py:242-249 hashes only dates[0]|dates[-1]|len(dates)|n_symbols|sample sizes) and Partura's PanelSet.view_id (panels.py:216, feeding sha1(view_id|expr_key) at :222). After a daily-field rebuild the first serves stale rank fingerprints -- a ban refusing candidates it should not -- and the second serves a stale on-disk panel for any DF:-bearing expression. Neither fails loudly. Only search-usability fixes the first (AC-12, and it warns that dropping it as plumbing ships the bug); only minimal-diff spots the second. If the exemplar cache is too expensive to invalidate, the operational rule (rebuild -> clear) has to be enforced by the build script, not left in a risk list.

dag.Node.is_leaf (dag.py:39-40), _load_leaf_cube (engine.py:227), _leaf_panel (engine.py:208) and _run_panel_round.operand (engine.py:356-363) must land in ONE commit. I confirmed the trap: _p_eligible reads node.spec.face with no None guard (schedule.py:57-58) so an unwidened is_leaf gives AttributeError on NoneType, and its elementwise branch admits `c.is_leaf and c.shape.degenerate`, so div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap) -- the headline turnover factor -- is scheduled into a P round and dies on RuntimeError('panel operand DF:FloatCap unavailable') if only the cube loader is patched. Under tolerant=True that is a silently dropped tree, not an error. All three designs identify this; it is listed here because the half-fix passes any test suite built around the in_expand / S-round example, and minimal-diff names it as the single most likely implementation miss.

A registry latch that makes op() raise after the first build_registry() (typed-correctness) needs a documented reset, or it breaks the suite's own throwaway-@op tests -- conftest.py's `registry` fixture is session-scoped (tests/conftest.py:8-9), so by the time a real_valued=True test kernel registers, the registry is closed, and the same plan also asserts the latch fires. It also imposes a call-order change on scripts/idea_search.py, which imports ops_ext at module level and parses seeds through parse(...) before run_mining. search-usability's weaker guard (load_plugins raises when catalog._DEFAULT is not None) catches the real hazard -- a plugin loaded after the registry was built, silently 45 operators short -- without either side effect; prefer that form, and drop Partura's catalog._DEFAULT = None reset either way.
